lesson_title: The Price List of Hours: Gross Pay, Scales and Overtime
hook_text: Why is a Sunday hour worth DOUBLE a Tuesday hour? Payroll has a price list.
clip_script: Why should one hour ever cost more than another hour? Stand in the worker's shoes on a Sunday morning. The whole street is sleeping in; you are signing for a delivery. Your ordinary hour costs the shop fifty rand — but this is not an ordinary hour. This is your weekend, your family's time, your rest. So the price list has three rows. Ordinary hours: fifty rand — the plain price. Evening or Saturday overtime: seventy-five rand — time and a half, a small apology stapled to every hour. Sundays and public holidays: DOUBLE — one hundred rand — because those are the hours that cost you most to give. Before touching the hours, write down the price of that kind of hour. The row first, every time.
visual_style: A glowing three-row price list building up beside a ticking clock; coins stack higher as the rows change from plain to time-and-a-half to double.
pacing: Three clear beats, one per price row, closing fast on the rule.
